key_claim: FERC's E-1 order in Docket RD26-7-000 directs NERC, under section 215(d)(5) of the Federal Power Act, to develop and submit new or modified Reliability Standards for computational-load integration and revisions to its Rules of Procedure including registry criteria for computational load entities, both due by 31 December 2026.
frame_summary: FERC argues that the reliability risks of integrating computational loads into the bulk-power system require mandatory standards and registry criteria delivered on a fixed deadline, not voluntary industry timelines.
verbatim_quote: The order directs North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), pursuant to section 215(d)(5) of the Federal Power Act, to develop and submit new or modified Reliability Standards addressing the reliability risks associated with the integration of computational loads into the Bulk-Power System.
verbatim_list: The Commission also directs NERC to develop revisions to its Rules of Procedure, including registry criteria for computational load entities.
Both The Reliability Standards and Rules of Procedure revisions are due by December 31, 2026.

title: Level 3 Alert - Essential Action to Industry: Computational Load Modeling, Studies, Instrumentation, Commissioning, Operations, Protection, and Control
key_claim: NERC's highest-urgency Level 3 Alert directs transmission planners, owners, operators, reliability coordinators and balancing authorities to take seven Essential Actions on the modeling, study, commissioning, ride-through protection and communications of computational loads, with acknowledgement required by 11 May 2026 and reporting by 3 August 2026.
frame_summary: NERC argues that registered entities lack the processes to manage computational loads and must take immediate essential actions now, while it builds the registry criteria and standards that will bring the loads themselves under mandatory regulation.
verbatim_quote: In the responses provided to the Alert, NERC found that entities generally did not have sufficient processes, procedures, or methods to address risks associated with computational loads.
verbatim_list: Currently, this would include loads that are 20 MW and greater, connected at 60kV, and contain more than 1 MW of IT Load.
Reporting Required by Midnight Eastern on August 3, 2026

TOs should coordinate with computational load customers, where possible, on customer-side improvements to maximize the computational load facility-level “ride-through” performance up to equipment capability limitations to increase stability margins.

title: Standard Authorization Request: Reliability Standards to Address Computational Load - Phase I (Project 2026-02)

title: FERC Orders Mandatory NERC Reliability Standards for Data Center and Other Computational Loads
key_claim: FERC's 16 July order converts NERC's voluntary schedule into an enforceable requirement, with standards due 31 December 2026 and a Phase II work plan by 1 March 2027, and for the first time opens the door to registering loads as entities directly accountable under Section 215 of the Federal Power Act.
frame_summary: POWER frames the order as a watershed that extends the post-2005 mandatory reliability regime beyond generators and wires to consumption itself, with the documented Virginia and Texas load-loss events as the evidentiary trigger.
verbatim_quote: which documented a July 10, 2024 event in the Eastern Interconnection in which a 230 kV transmission line fault triggered six successive faults and the near-simultaneous loss of roughly 1,500 MW of data-center load, briefly pushing system frequency to 60.047 Hz.
verbatim_list: found that crypto-mining facilities can lose between 17% and 95% of pre-disturbance consumption within milliseconds of a normally cleared transmission fault.

“Certain large loads like data centers and crypto mining operations that NERC calls computational load have the potential to change their demand almost instantly,” FERC Chairman Laura Swett noted during the commission’s open meeting. “And this rapid fluctuation causes voltage stability issues that threaten grid reliability.”

The directive serves as a crucial step that brings computational loads—until now treated primarily as ordinary customers on the distribution side—under the mandatory reliability framework that has governed generators and transmission owners since Congress made NERC’s standards enforceable through the Energy Policy Act of 2005.
has determined that it must act now to mitigate the risks associated with large computational loads

proposed standards and glossary revisions are scheduled for release in August for a 45-day stakeholder comment period, followed by another comment period in October if needed. NERC expects to seek Board approval on Dec. 5 and file the final package with FERC by Dec. 31.
For the first time, the directive also opens the door to registering the loads themselves as entities directly accountable under Section 215 of the Federal Power Act.

mandates that NERC must also propose changes to its Rules of Procedure, including registry criteria for bringing computational-load entities directly under the mandatory reliability framework, and file a Phase II work plan for additional standards by March 1, 2027.
On Thursday, all five FERC commissioners voted for the order.

title: NERC issues Level 3 alert, mandates action to address data center load losses
key_claim: NERC's rare Level 3 alert, its highest level, requires grid entities to take seven actions by 3 August 2026 in response to data centres unexpectedly dropping load or oscillating demand; the last Level 3 alert, a year earlier, concerned inverter-based resources.
frame_summary: Utility Dive frames the Level 3 alert as a rare escalation that imposes near-term obligations on grid entities because data-centre load-loss events are outrunning existing planning and commissioning practice.
verbatim_quote: The alert includes seven actions grid entities “must implement to address immediate risks posed by computational loads,” NERC said.
verbatim_list: Registered NERC entities must acknowledge receipt by May 11 and must respond by Aug. 3.
“The grid faces unprecedented challenges from a surge in large power consumers,” NERC said in a statement.
Computational loads pose “immediate risks,” the grid watchdog said.
